title: Pawns Together Strong
reviewNotes: Montages, captions and native complete diagrams reviewed. Begin after Bxa5 at 84 seconds, the complete eight-piece source diagram White Kh1/e6 against Kd3/Ba5/c6/d5/g6/h5. Native16/17 confirm a5/Bxa5 and native18 confirms e7. e7 is the last illustrated move; every following Black reply and promotion continuation in this lesson is independent representative analysis, not recovered source play. A complete finite White strategy checks every Black response to e7, promotes immediately when legal and reaches exact supported seven-piece wins through actual captures within five plies. All four black pawns and the bishop remain until legally captured; no piece is discarded to fit tablebase coverage. The bishop is on a5, unlike the separately analyzed b4/b6 source versions. The earlier h5/g6/Nb4 sacrifices and alternative acceptance choices remain outside this selected proof; all earlier drafts, partial probes and review decisions remain preserved.
transcript: I love this chess puzzle because it really goes to show how powerful pawns are once they start collaborating. In this position, it seems like there's no way to make progress for white. Every single pawn is stopped by one of black's pawns. This knight is not going to be as good as this bishop at picking up the opponent's pawn. So, it seems like if anyone is playing for an advantage, it's black. But, as you can imagine, since we're here, that's not the case. White in this position actually has a forced win with H5. Of course, if black doesn't do anything, this pawn is going to queen. So, black has to take the pawn. But now we follow up with G6. Another pawn sacrifice. And once again, black has to accept the sacrifice. But now the E pawn is going to be able to walk. E6. Now, the only move that stops the promotion is bishop A3. But here comes the brilliancancy. Knight B4, a full knight sacrifice. And the point is that if the king takes, now we've gained one precious tempo where the bishop is blocked and we're going to be able to get a new queen. And if the bishop takes, well, now we're able to push the A pawn. And bishops are known for being terrible at stopping two pawns at the same time because now on the next move, we'll be able to just start walking with A5. And if the bishop takes this pawn, we're going to be able to promote the other one and win the [Music]
